The drought event across the USVI is a concern to agricultural interests, as hot and dry days increase water demands, while stressing pastures, crops and native vegetation. Additionally, the groundwater reserves kept decreasing. Some agricultural interests are buying up to 3000 gallons of water daily to keep their products relatively healthy. Ranchers are also buying other supplements for the livestock. The hey to feet of the horses is scarce. A fire ban is now in effect for all the territory.

events.event_narrative: Above normal precipitation was received across the northern Virgin Islands during September, and the severe drought conditions were erased along these areas. In general, over 6 inches of rain fell during the month, with a few isolated areas receiving around 15 inches.

Drought conditions improved below severe criteria during September, mainly due to rains brought by Hurricane Fiona. However, the island remained under Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions for the rest of the month.

The precursor of Hurricane Earl brought above normal rainfalls for the eastern half of Puerto Rico during the first few days of the month. These rains resulted in drought improvement below Severe Drought (D2) criteria. By the mid to latter part of the month, additional rainfalls, mainly due to Hurricane Fiona, resulted in the removal of all drought categories across the territory.

events.cz_name: ST. THOMAS / ST. JOHN AND ADJACENT ISLANDS
events.event_narrative: The official ASOS station, as well as several other unofficial stations across St. Thomas and St. John frequently reported heat indices values of at least 108F degrees for at least two hours. These stations reported values of 112 or more several days of the month, which meets the criteria for Excessive Heat Warning.

Farmers are reporting  that rain is not penetrating the soil due to evaporation from heat and wind. The U.S.V.I. Department of Agriculture is buying and storing hay and providing water. Poultry farmers also report that they are concerned that guinea grass is sparce and poultry are not eating grain. There is a smaller number of egg production. These reports led the U.S. Drought Monitor to classify the island as Exceptionally Dry (D4).

events.cz_name: ST. THOMAS / ST. JOHN AND ADJACENT ISLANDS
events.event_narrative: Farmers are reporting that ponds are evaporating due to high heat. Planting has been reduced. Livestock farmers are separating males and females to reduce births due to the lack of forage land. They are also buying grain and hay for the animals. These conditions led the U.S. Drought monitor to classify the island of St. Thomas under Exceptional Drought (D4), while a Severe Drought (D3) was also introduced to St. John by the middle of the month.
Rains and low visibilities were recorded at the Saint Croix airport. Light to moderate rain was recorded during the period from 1900 AST on the 14th of August through 7 am AST August 15.
Rain and low visibilities were recorded by the Saint Thomas ASOS. Light to moderate rain was recorded between 2300 AST on the 14th of August through 9 am AST on the 15 of August.

Periods of heavy rain with low visibilities were recorded at the San Juan airport. Light rain began around 2300 AST on the 14th of August and varied between light and moderate through the night and ended around 1100 AST on the 15th of August. Rainfall accumulations of around 2.27 inches were recorded.

events.cz_name: ST. THOMAS / ST. JOHN AND ADJACENT ISLANDS
events.event_narrative: With the rains received at the end of the month, Saint John is now free of any drought, while St. Thomas improved from Exceptional Drought (D4) to a Severe Drought (D2). Based on observations from the wells monitored by the USGS, well levels remain low at St. Thomas.

Flooding was occurring at PR-160 in direction toward Pueblo Nuevo since Rio Cibuco was out of it banks. A car was reported trapped in this flooding.
Flooding was reported at Carretera del Collage in Manati. A car was trapped in the waters.
Emergency Managers indicated flooding nears Willys Pizza and Puente Bull. The low level crossing was impassable, but the road was closed without people being directly affected.
A small landslide was reported near road PR-2 in Arecibo, close to the funeral home Cristo Rey.
A forest fire that developed in San German consumed near 4 acres of terrain. Two individuals were affected by smoke inhalation and were transported to the hospital.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS EAST OF PUERTO RICO, AROUND VIEQUES, AND AROUND AND JUST NORTH OF CULEBRA AND SAINT JOHN
events.event_narrative: A TV meteorologist shared a picture in social media of a well defined waterspout south of Vieques.
Flooding was reported at Calle 11 in Salinas, next to Highway PR-52.The report indicated that a residence was being affected.
Downed power lines were reported on road 1 Ramal 543.

A 40-year-old male tourist and his two daughters were swept away by rip currents at Montones Beach in Isabela. The man managed to rescue the girls but was also dragged and unable to get out of the water. Paramedics from State Medical Emergencies provided first aid and confirmed that the individual no longer had vital signs.

A family of seven was swept away by rip currents in Playa Escondida, Fajardo. The father was able to save all his children and wife, but he drowned, and his body was recovered two days later in the area.

Two males were swept away by rip currents near Ventana del Mar, behind La Concha Hotel in Condado. According to initial reports, a local resident tried to rescue a tourist who had been pulled away by the currents. They both drowned. The first victim was identified as a 20-year-old male from Washington visiting the island for Spring Break. The second victim was a staff sergeant in the Puerto Rico Army National Guard, his body was recovered three miles from the beach two days later on March 12.

A rip current swept away a 52-year-old male tourist from Minnesota at La Pared Beach in Luquillo on March 13th. The person was rescued and taken to the Caribbean Medical Center in critical condition, where he died.

A rescue operation began on March 28 for a 26-year-old tourist, an active duty U.S. marine, and a resident of Massachusetts who was swept away by rip currents on La Pared beach in Luquillo on March 27. The Coast Guard rescue crews suspended search efforts on April 1 in support of local emergency response agencies. He is presumed dead.

events.event_narrative: A fair-weather waterspout with a spray ring was spotted from Humacao along a streamer of clouds downwind from Vieques.

The residents along Calle Theopolis in Mayaguez shared with a TV meteorologist (which was then confirmed with Mayaguez's Emergency Managers) that flooding was affecting their neighborhood. The Doppler radar estimated between 2 and 3 inches of rain due to strong thunderstorms, which was the leading cause of the flooding problem observed, mainly along the road.

A strong thunderstorm produced heavy rains that triggered a mudslide along road PR-105 in Sector Margarita, Barrio Lim��n, at Mayaguez, making it impassable���the Doppler radar rainfall estimated around 2 inches of rain during the event.

A tropical wave increased local moisture and instability, boosting local effects and enhancing the formation of an intense thunderstorm, which resulted in the pea-sized hail event. The social media post was validated with the weather data and residents of Barrio Voladora in Moca.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS EAST OF PUERTO RICO, AROUND VIEQUES, AND AROUND AND JUST NORTH OF CULEBRA AND SAINT JOHN
events.event_narrative: A waterspout was sighted just east of Hotel El Conquistador in Fajardo. The waterspout looked very week on the video.

A video shared in social media showed significant rapid moving water along Camino El Duque. The video showed water reaching the low levels of a house and covering the wheels of a car, about one foot deep.
The entrance toward Cuesta del Leon community in Barrio Casablanca was impassable as a stream was out of its banks. Vegetation debris was observed clogging the bridge.
Flooding was observed along Zona Industrial in Carolina. The video showed flood waters about 18 inches deep. A Honda HRV was stranded. Vehicles were able to move through, but with great difficulty.
A long segment of PR-31 was shown as flooded, as well as the farms surrounding the streets. The road looked impassable, but with no vehicles or structures being affected.

Stagnant flooding waters were observed in a video shared in social media along Calle Colon in San Juan. The depth of the water looked about two feet, reaching the entrance, but not inside, of the nearby residences.
Flooding was observed in front of Fine Arts in Munoz Rivera Avenue in Hato Rey, San Juan. The avenue was still passable, but it was slowing down traffic.
A 40-year-old male tourist from Michigan drowned at La Cueva del Indio, near road PR-681 in the Islote sector of Arecibo. According to reports, he was caught in a rip        current.
Emergency Managers reported coastal flooding near Barranquitas St. in Mirador-Peatonal, Condado.
A video through social media reported flooding in the streets of Joffre, Marseille, Piccioni, and Delcasse in the Condado neighborhood, impacting residents and infrastructure.

Coastal erosion caused the collapse of segments of the Paseo de la Laguna pedestrian and cyclist pathway near Ramon Baldorioty de Castro Ave, posing risks to pathway users and adjacent infrastructure.

Several broadcast media sources reported damage in Marginal el Paseo Victor Rojas due to strong swell action and beach erosion. The municipal police closed several streets, including Cervantes St., Los Pinos St., and Adriano Gonzalez, St.

Coastal flooding was reported in Ashford Ave, near the intersection with Delcasse St. No people were reported trapped. At 12 PM Buoy 41053, around 2 miles northwest, reported a significant wave height of 7.7 ft from the northeast with a period of 10.5 seconds. High tide (1.84 ft) was at 10:28 AM.
Coastal erosion reported along Paseo Lineal in PR-25 N Ave. Luis Munoz Rivera after intersection with General Esteves St. in San Juan. Part of the old linear path fell off into the water.
Honda Creek out of its banks flooded PR-31, KM14.9, leaving both lanes impassable. This is near Edgardo Auto Parts and the intersection with PR-936.
A completely flooded roadway was reported at PR-2, KM76 near a fast food restaurant, a beauty supply and a shopping center due to poor drainage. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
Emergency Managers reported that PR-2, KM 84.0 (Jose Joaquin Yiye Avila St.) in front of El Buen Cafe Restaurant was completely flooded with both lanes impassable.
The 911 Call Center reported a car partly submerged in flood waters from rio Blanco, with one person trapped inside, near PR-31, KM 8.2, Dr. Jose Barbosa highway.

Public shared a video in social media of a Sink Hole in a bridge (over Jacaboa river) along road PR-7755 in Bo. Jacaboa in Patillas due to heavy rain. Several Families are uncommunicated due to the situation. Approximately 2-3 inches have fallen combined with previous rainfall.
Flooding was reported along road PR-2, KM 87.7 near Hatillo Town Center. No injuries or fatalities were reported.

A landslide occurred in PR-198, near Francisco Torres School and the Emilio Huyke double-A baseball park in Las Piedras, affecting one lane of the roadway.
A stranded vehicle was reported in PR-2 in Manati near Villa Maria Shopping Center.

events.event_narrative: A waterspout was reported by several members of the public near Annies Place Restaurant and Combate beach, Cabo Rojo. It lasted around 10 minutes and a Spray Ring was visible and recorded.

PR-987, KM 4.8, in Bo. Las Croabas was impassable due to flooding. The road was closed by officials during the early morning hours.

No injuries were reported among the 5 residents of the home, including a child, an 88-year-old man, and a 78-year-old woman. The home showed badly damaged walls and columns, as well as a sinkhole in the floor. Emergency managers reported that the home and surrounding land are 5 feet deep from before the landslide.
Leftover debris along bridge in road PR-31 km 6.3 due a previous stream overflowing. A |Flash Flood Warning was in effect when reported.

Emergency managers reported a landslide affecting a portion of road PR-901 in Barrio Camino Nuevo, near km 8.3. The road was also blocked by a large boulder.

The left lane of PR-53 (Dr. Jose C. Barbosa Highway), km 12.3, south towards Humacao, was closed due to a landslide.
A landslide was blocking a lane on PR-908, km 10.5, in Jagueyes, Yabucoa.

Flooding was reported in PR-979 (Lauro Pinero Ave.) in Ceiba. Heavy rain over the roof on an old building near a Barber Shop, caused part of the roof to collapse.
Rio Candelero, near sector Los Rodriguez in Bo. Candelero Arriba, Humacao was out of its banks and flooding nearby roads.

Around 8:44 PM on November 16, 2024, a 63-year-old male and his passenger, a 39-year-old woman, crossed a low-level crossing/bridge in Barrio Guayabota, Sector Sasa, particularly on road 182 km 12. This bridge was covered with water as Guayanes River went over it due to the heavy rainfall activity that the municipality of Yabucoa was receiving. Radar estimates and observations suggested around 2 to 4 inches of rain in the area of the incident and around 6 inches across the municipality. As they crossed the bridge, the Ford F-150 that they were in got dragged into the fast-flowing river. During this event, the woman was trapped in the vehicle, that became lodged under rubble, and drowned.
PR-53 (Dr. Jose Celso Barbosa Highway) in exit PR-10, at the bridge, was reported as flooded and unpassable with several vehicles trapped.
Tarawa St. was reported as intransitable due to flooding with several vehicles trapped.
PR-976, km 2, near Juan Diego Creek in Fajardo was reported as flooded with several vehicles trapped.
PR-52, exit 21, towards PR-172 were reported as flooded and impassable. This is near the Menonita Hospital in Caguas.
Areas near Hogar Cristo Rey in Ave. Degetou, were reported as flooded.
On PR-3, km 92.3, in Sector Aguacate from the old Winston Building to the old Union Carbide Building, a nearby river overflowed its banks and was blocking a passage through the road.
Flooding was reported in PR-31, Juncos, near the intersection with PR-9185. That sector of the road was closed due to it being impassable.
The 911 Call Center reported a flooded house in El Cemi Public Housing, Building 4, Luquillo. This was Apartment 49 of that complex. No injuries nor fatalities were reported.
Cruz Ortiz Estela Ave. was reported as flooded, near the local Tax Office, Dufresne St., and Luis Munoz Marin Ave. A building was affected.
A house flooded in Girasol St. in Los Sauces Urb., due to a nearby creek over it's banks.
Road PR-936 to PR-31 in Barrio Boqueron was closed due to flooding. A sector of the road, over a local creek, was impassable.
Flooding was reported in PR-3, just in front of Walmart in Punta Santiago. Several people were trapped inside different vehicles due to the inundation.
Flooding in Street 14 in Urb. Villa Humacao affected a house.
Adriatico street in Urb. Palacios del Mar was flooded. At least 1 house was reported as affected.

Several reports confirmed that PR-3 next to the Palma Real Shopping Center was impassable due to flooding, leaving transiting automobiles stuck on the road. Flooding was also reported within the parking of the Shopping Center. Images reveal water above most of the wheel on various cars.
Flooding was reported on video at PR-923 near Buena Vista Urb. At least 5 stuck cars due to flooding were observed with the rest of the traffic moving very slowly.
Rosalinda St. was reported flooded, this flood reached a house and trapped people inside.
Tinajera creek went out of its banks, leaving the nearby PR-927 impassable.
PR-906 and Tejas Ave. were reported as flooded, near a local police station and a Burlington store.
PR-924 was reported as flooded just in front of the Munagorry Perfume Store in Humacao.
A landslide was reported at PR-149 in Orocovis, near KM 40.5, the closed business La Bodega de Las Brujas, and the Dona Juana Waterfall.
A 68-year-old man from Connecticut, a resident of Culebra, was last seen being dragged by a rip current at Flamenco Beach, Culebra. His body was found after two days.

A 90-year-old resident in Luquillo and a visitor from Utah, USA, was found dead, likely due to drowning, approximately 30 miles offshore from Costa Azul in Luquillo. The incident occurred around 5 PM AST on Christmas Day, and Emergency Managers initiated the search and rescue mission with the US Coast Guard after he was reported missing at 9:30 PM. According to reports from Luquillo's Emergency Management director and the US Coast Guard, it is believed that he died after being caught in a rip current that dragged him out to sea.

A 63-year-old man was fishing with his son at a boat ramp near Playa Abacoa, close to the mouth of Ca��o Tiburones in Arecibo. At approximately 5:40 AM AST, the man lost his footing and fell into the water, where strong rip currents swiftly carried him into open waters. His son immediately alerted emergency services, leading to a rapid mobilization of local resources, including the U.S. Coast Guard. Later that day, his shoe and baseball cap were discovered approximately a mile and a half offshore. The search efforts continued until the afternoon of January 20 (the following day), when his body was found near Club Nautico de Arecibo at around 3 PM.
A landslide was reported by Emergency Managers in the interior side of Los Millonarios St. (St. 1) in Arecibo. No people were reported as trapped or injured.
Road 130 closed due to flooding near Lechuga Bakery, Lechuga Pharmacy, and Texaco Gas Station 518. Radar estimates indicated around 2 inches close to 3 inches.

OMME Quebradillas informed that the intersection between St. 2 in Bo. Cocos, Quebradillas, and PR-2 (Jose Joaquin Yiye Avila St.) was closed due to flooding. This             was also between HAS Auto Parts and San Rafael COOP.
A professor from the University of Puerto Rico reported sand and vegetation along PR-102 near the Guanajibo River due to large breaking waves in the area.

Severe coastal erosion caused by strong wave action from an incoming swell has impacted the intersection of Cll 10 and Cll 3 in Parcelas Suarez, Loiza. By morning, broadcast media showed parts of the road edge destroyed. By afternoon, emergency managers reported continued erosion with the road completely impassable, leaving only one heavily undermined lane.

Emergency managers reported coastal flooding and debris deposition in the Cerro Gordo area of Vega Alta. The provided photo shows a flooded residential street, with standing water and scattered debris. The flooding and debris are associated with strong wave action from an incoming swell impacting the coast.

A COCORAHS observer reported a funnel cloud around Bayamon. The funnel cloud lasted less than 5 minutes, and it was observed moving west-northwestward.
The 911 call center reported flooding along Calle 22 affecting Residencia C-1 in Barrio Quebrada Vuelta in Fajardo.
The 911 call center reported a stranded car due to flooding along Avenida Las Palmas near Iglesia de Dios Primitiva and Rest Chino Jo King Chinese.
Public reports on social media that PR-172 near Garaje Rafy Transmission was partially flooded.
The 911 call center reported flooding along Calle Marginal 110 in Condominio San Francisco, Bayam��n. The parking lot was flooded with stranded cars.
The 911 call center reported flooding in several sections of road PR-784 in Barrio Canaboncito, Sector La Vega, near Escuela Andres Rosales.
The 911 call center reported floodwaters entering house L-2 in Urbanizaci��n Villa Sauri, Calle 1, Caguas.
The 911 call center reported floodwaters entering a house at Calle San Lorenzo 36 in Catano.
A member of the public uploaded a video showing Ro Loco beginning to overflow and impacting PR-365, with water starting to cover a low-level crossing.
A 911 reporter informed us that a house at 53 Victoria Road in the urban area of Anasco is experiencing flooding. There are people reportedly trapped.
A 911 reporter reported that a house along Road 411 in Aguada was affected by flooding. The property is next to a river.
A 911 reporter informed us that Road Tetu��n in the urban area of Anasco is flooded.
A member of the public reported significant flooding affecting a house and vehicles on Calle Nueva in Bo. Mayuco, Anasco.
Emergency manager reported flooding over PR-171 KM 6.1 in Bo Rincon Sector La Linea due to floodwaters from Rio La Plata.
A social media post reported a flooded road in Camino Municipal near a restaurant called El Kapotazo due to excessive runoff and a small stream in the area.
Ro Cibuco overflowed its banks and affected Road 620 in Vega Alta. The road was impassable.
Flooding is affecting the area where PR 419 intersects with PR 2 near the Hyatt Place, Manati. The road remained closed.
Emergency manager reports stranded cars due to flooding waters over PR-2 at km 83 in Arecibo.
Flooding affected the road and garage entrance of several houses in Sector La Guinea in Arecibo.
Flooding impacted multiple lanes on Ave. Juan Ponce de Le��n in San Juan, directly in front of Island Finance Bank.
An emergency manager reported a lightning strike incident involving a 17-year-old female in Bo, Santa Rosa sector La 15. The individual was stable and conscious at the regional hospital in Arecibo.
An emergency manager reported that PR-2, near an auto dealer, was impassable due to poor drainage. Two vehicles were stranded and rescued by local officers.
Emergency managers reported flooding on Calle Las Canelas after Quebrada Seca, a small stream, overflowed its banks.
Emergency managers reported flooding at Angel Sandin Martinez Middle School and its adjacent roads.
Emergency managers reported flooding on PR-2 near the intersection with PR-160 and above Rio Cibuco.
Emergency managers reported flooding on Guarico Avenue, near the intersection with Hector Pantojas St., caused by a local creek overflowing its banks. The road was not reported as impassable.
The 911 call center reported flooding on PR-102 in Barrio Pueblo, near the Almacen Navide��o. One female was trapped in a car.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM CABO SAN JUAN TO THE WATERS BETWEEN ANEGADA ISLAND AND VIRGIN GORDA AND NORTH 10 NM
events.event_narrative: Broadcast media shared a user-submitted video on social media showing a funnel cloud  observed from Playa Flamenco in Culebra. The funnel cloud appeared to be located northeast of the beach. A second witness confirmed the event, observing it from Fajardo during the afternoon hours.
Debris flow was reported near the intersection of PR-164 & PR-159, in Corozal. This debris flow was reported as only affecting the roadway.
Broadcast media reported that a man drowned after being swept away by rip currents in Playa Jobos (Jobos Beach) in Isabela.
Flash flooding was reported in the Ponce Bypass area (main street) near Highway PR 2, with radar estimates indicating approximately 1 to 3 inches of rainfall.
Flash flooding was reported along PR 52 near Urb. Los Caobos, with radar estimates indicating approximately 1 to 4 inches of rainfall.
Flash flooding was reported along PR 14 near La Rambla Pizza House and San Lucas Hospital, with radar estimates indicating approximately 1 to 4 inches of rainfall.
Water entered the first floor of Mercedita Airport in Ponce. Radar estimates indicate approximately 1 to 4 inches of rainfall in the area.

Bayam��n emergency managers reported that Calle 8 (8th Street) in Santa Rosa is flooded due to heavy rains and poor drainage. No vehicles or homes were affected, only the water on the roadway. This road is over a tributary to Rio Hondo (River).
Emergency management reported that Ram��n Luis Rivera Avenue, near a Walgreens pharmacy, was flooded but passable due to poor drainage. The report did not include whether any vehicles were stranded.
Flash flooding was reported at PR-869 and Flor del Valle Avenue in front of Sullivans BBQ. A car was stranded in the flooding waters with two people trapped inside.
The 911 call center reported that one person was trapped in their home due to urban flooding in Urb. Santa Rosa, 17th Street, Block 15.
Flooding was reported at Calle Acueducto (St. 833) towards Lincoln Park Condominium.
Flooding was reported in Monserrate Deliz Street in Toa Baja near the Antiguo Rio de Bayamon (River), no people nor vehicles were reported as trappped.
Flooding was reported in Street 3 (Santa Clara Street) in Fajardo. Flooding was reported in one house. No one was trapped.
Debris flow under saturated soils promoted resulted in a fallen tree on Road 139 at KM 18.2 in Sector Carmelita in Ponce.

A broadcast media meteorologist shared a video of a medium to large branch falling            from a tree near a parking lot on PR-125 (Ave. Emerito Estrada Rivera), at the border of Barrio Pueblo and Barrio Bahomamey, due to a strong thunderstorm that developed ove the area.
Social media post reported a damaged building roof edge at the Condado Real  Condominium in Kings Court Street & McLeary Avenue.

The 911 Call Center and Emergency Managers reported that 2 female minors and 1 female adult were injured by a lightning strike at the  Balneario Seven Seas, Fajardo, near PR-987 (Cabezas St.). The female minors were reported as stable, conscious and breathing at the time of the report. One of the minors age was not reported but the other one was reported as being 16 years old. The female adult was 21 years old.
Debris Flow was reported in PR-183 (Jesus Sta. Aponte St.) close to the Pedro Rivera Molina Elementary School. No vehicles or people were reported as trapped.
Street flooding was reported in the northeast section of Bayamon.
Minor wind damage was reported at Urb. Vivoni in San German.
Urban flooding was reported in Cupey, Bayamon, and Guaynabo. The Rio Piedras river was near one foot above flood stage upstream.
Period of heavy rain affected Saint Croix from mid morning through early afternoon. Urban flooding was reported across the island. A resident of western Saint Croix reported 1.18 inches rainfall.

NOAA Crews Station at Salt River, Saint Croix recorded strong gusty winds during the morning and early afternoon. A peak wind of 46 knots was recorded at 11 am. The Saint Croix airport ASOS sensor recorded a peak gust of 37 knots at 1054 am.
A 31-year-old male was surfing on August 24th near Kikita Beach Dorado, when he was swept by rip currents. His body was recovered on Tuesday (August 26th) morning.
On August 24th, a man climbed onto a rocky area at Mar Chiquita, Manati, when a wave swept him, and he fell into the sea. His body was recovered the next morning.

US Coast Guard watchstanders received a report of four surfers in distress at Playa Los Tubos, Manati. Watchstanders also coordinated with Manat�� Office of Emergency Management and Puerto Rico Police Joint Forces of Rapid Action in Vega Baja. Despite challenging marine conditions, all four surfers were injured but were rescued safely.
A lifeguard assisted a person in distress who was swept away by a rip current in San Juan. The injured person was rescued and taken to the hospital.

A man was swept away by rip currents and drowned this morning at Chatarra beach in Loiza, near PR-187 and the local kiosks. His body was recovered by a Coast Guard helicopter, taken to Isla Grande Airport, and then to the Hoare Hospital in Santurce, where he was declared dead.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM CABO SAN JUAN TO THE WATERS BETWEEN ANEGADA ISLAND AND VIRGIN GORDA AND NORTH 10 NM
events.event_narrative: Social media reports from Barriada Clark indicated a short-lived waterspout north of Playa Flamenco in Culebra.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS EAST OF PUERTO RICO, AROUND VIEQUES, AND AROUND AND JUST NORTH OF CULEBRA AND SAINT JOHN
events.event_narrative: Social Media photos reported a funnel cloud near the coast between Naguabo & Ceiba, around 3.6 miles SE from the coast.

Emergency managers reported flooding from waters of Quebrada Berrench��n, affecting a portion of PR-335 around KM 0.5, near the Water Treatment Plant in Yauco. The road became temporarily impassable and was closed by emergency managers.

The 911 Call Center reported flooding affecting houses on Jose M. Tartak Street in   Carolina. No people were reported trapped. Based on radar estimates, between 1.5 to 2 inches of rain had fallen by 4:37 PM.

The 911 Call Center reported that at approximately 3:20 PM AST, a lightning strike impacted two individuals in a boat near the fishing club by the dam at Lago Toa Vaca. One individual was reported conscious with burns to the hands but breathing. The second individual, a 48 year old male, was thrown into the water by the impact; his body was found at around 8 PM ast.

A NWS employee and emergency managers, reported a lightning strike that impacted electrical lines near KM 3.0 of PR-725 in the Los Pinos sector of Barrio Llanos. The incident caused a utility pole to fall and scattered debris in the area, resulting in a power outage.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS EAST OF PUERTO RICO, AROUND VIEQUES, AND AROUND AND JUST NORTH OF CULEBRA AND SAINT JOHN
events.event_narrative: Broadcast media shared a photo on social media of a waterspout observed around 5.2 miles SE from Maunabo.

Aguada Emergency Management officials reported flooding due to a small stream overflowing its banks near PR-115 at kilometer 21.5, in the vicinity of Cielo Mar Bakery. As a result, that area of PR-115 was impassable.
A small landslide was reported at PR-523, km 2.7. A tree was carried down by the landslide, and it got tangled between the power lines.

A member of the public reported to the 911 Call Center that a tree, along with power lines, fell next to Establo Modesto Espinosa on Road 689, due to convective weather near that area. The incident is currently obstructed traffic.

Heavy rainfall caused the Rio Blanco to rise out of its banks, resulting in localized flooding along La Pitina curve in Naguabo. One person was stranded by rapidly rising water but was rescued safely by the Naguabo Municipal Office of Emergency Management. Only the La Pitina curve was flooded; nearby exit 22 remained open to traffic.
Emergency managers reported that PR-103 was partially flooded due to overflow from  Rio Guanajibo.
Emergency managers reported that floodwaters from the Rio Culebrinas are affected PR-418 (Camino Coloso) near LUMA Energy, prompting the closure of the road to the public.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS FROM CABO SAN JUAN TO THE WATERS BETWEEN ANEGADA ISLAND AND VIRGIN GORDA AND NORTH 10 NM
events.event_narrative: A pilot passenger posted a video on social media, capturing a well-formed waterspout northeast of Culebrita at around 5 PM AST.
Emergency managers reported that the bridge in Street 14 above Canal Marta (Channel) was impassable due to a sudden rise of the channel's level.
Emergency managers called to report an impassable primary road PR-177 (Lomas Verdes Avenue) near a Costco Wholesale store due to a sudden rise of Rio Bayamon (river).

A member of the public contacted the 911 Center to report flooding at the end of Road 3, near San Ignacio Avenue and PR-199. Approximately 1 to 4 inches of rainfall had been recorded by 3 PM (time of the report). There were no reports of water entering homes or causing damage to property.

The Emergency Manager reported that a creek located behind Larcoop Cooperative Bank in Utuado had overflowed its banks, affecting multiple roads near the area. Despite the  flooding, all affected roads remain passable. According to radar estimates, approximately 1 to 4 inches of rainfall had been reported by 4 PM.
Emergency managers reported flooding from the Rio Culebrinas affecting PR-115 in  Barrio Espinar. The road was subsequently closed to the public.

Large breaking waves during the day caused the collapse of the remaining structure of the iconic Crash Boat pier in Aguadilla due to swells from Hurricane Erin. Video and eyewitness reports in social media confirmed surf impacts leading to structural failure.
Partial flooding reported below the PR-22 bridge, at Central Juanita Ave., near the Federal Bureau Prison in Guaynabo.

Multiple damages reported on social media including fallen trees and branches, tents, and kiosks along Avenida Las Nereidas in Catano. Station nearby reported wind gusts around 45 mph. No injuries nor fatalities were reported.

The director of OMME San Juan reported that at around 4:00 PM at Plaza de las Palomas in Old San Juan, thunderstorm winds knocked down a large tree branch, striking an older woman who had to be assisted by emergency managers.
At around 4:00 PM, a thunderstorm caused strong winds that knocked down heavy concrete pots in the Paseo de la Princesa in Old San Juan, according to OMME San Juan.
Landslide affected road PR-111 near Cascada Salto Collazo (waterfall) in San Sebastian. The road was partially closed.
Traffic on the Luis A. Ferre Highway was affected due to a flooded lane near the Monumento al Jibaro Puertorriqueno. Rainfall at 8:39 AM was estimated at approximately 1 to 2 inches.
An emergency manager reported that the Boardwalk area and Jose Nasario Street in Guanica are impassable. Around 1 to 2 inches of rain had fallen by 10:50 AM.
Emergency Managers from Guanica indicated that the PR-121 low water crossing was closed due to flood waters from Rio Loco.
The 911 Call Center reported a fallen pole with power lines obstructing the roadway PR-181 at kilometer 10.4 in Barrio Dos  Bocas, Trujillo Alto.
The 911 Call Center reported a fallen tree and power lines obstructing PR-611 in Barrio  Sabana Grande.
A 911 caller reported a landslide affecting part of road 10 from Utuado to Adjuntas municipality. Around 0.5 inches of rain had fallen by the time of the report.

A power pole fell near the Borinquen Arecibo Cockpit on PR-123. Vehicle traffic through this area was affected. Around the time of the incident strong showers and thunderstorms were moving across the area with wind gusts around 23 to 25 mph.
A fallen tree has been reported by emergency managers near Cine Metro in Santurce, obstructing a portion of the roadway. This incident occurred as outer bands from Hurricane Erin moved onshore.

OMME Corozal reported via 911 that a fallen tree and power cables are blocking the roadway on PR-159, between kilometers 17.9 and 18.0, in the neighborhood line of Abras and Palmarejo. This incident occurred as the outer bands of Hurricane Erin moved onshore.

A fallen power pole and tree branches have been reported by the 911 Call Center via email, blocking the roadway on PR-5 in Bayamon. The obstruction is located just before the exit toward Avenida Los Millones. This incident occurred as the outer bands of Hurricane Erin moved onshore.

The 911 Call Center reported a fallen tree at PR-865, blocking the roadway. This was near the intersections with Palma St., Camajey St. & Tabonuco St. This incident occurred as the outer bands of Hurricane Erin moved onshore.

The 911 Call Center reported a fallen utility pole at Camino Concepcion Sanchez (Concepcion Sanchez Way) and blocking the roadway. Electrical cables were also reported as hanging and over the roadway. This incident occurred as the outer bands of Hurricane Erin moved onshore.

A fallen tree and a fallen utility pole were reported in Camino Ramiro Montanez (Ramiro Montanez Way) in Aguas Buenas. This was near the intersection with Camino Minillas (Minillas Way). The fallen tree was reported over a house and its balcony. Electric cables were also reported over the roadway and near the house.
The 911 Call Center reported a fallen tree near Avenida Degetau and PR-788. The tree is blocking the roadway, but there are no people trapped and no electrical cables in the area.
A tree fell along PR-2 near Centro Integral de Salud de Vega Alta and Escuela Ileana de Garcia. The tree is blocking the roadway, but there are no people trapped and no electrical cables in the area.

Broadcast media through social media reported a lightning strike that impacted a residence in the Bo. Lagunas sector of Aguada. Residents reported a loud explosion-like sound and a bright flash that woke people from sleep. Minor structural damage to a wall was observed. No injuries were reported. Lightning strike occurred within outer bands associated with Hurricane Erin.
A power line fell along Calle La Fe in Catano.
Power lines fell along Calle Saragoza intersecting Calle Barcelona near the park area.

Multiple trees were reported down across PR-374 in the Castaner sector of Lares during the afternoon. Social media reports and local officials confirm blocked roads and scattered power line impacts due to wind gusts associated with the outer bands of Hurricane Erin. Municipal emergency crews were working to clear debris.
A 911 report indicated that bamboo trees fell onto PR-30 near the exit to Exp. Chayanne in Gurabo. The roadway was obstructed. It was unknown if electrical lines were affected.

Municipal officials and local media reported multiple downed trees and power lines along PR-146 in Ciales during the afternoon close to km 23.6. Roads were blocked and emergency crews were dispatched to clear debris. Impacts were associated with gusty winds from Hurricane Erin's outer bands.
The 911 Call Center reported a fallen tree obstructing the primary roadway on PR-2, just past the Walgreens in Plaza Victoria. No injuries or trapped individuals have been reported.

A 911 Call center report indicated a tree down along PR-2, close to km 131.1. The tree obstructed the roadway. Emergency management were dispatched to the scene. Impacts were associated with gusty winds from the outer bands of Hurricane Erin.

A 911 caller reported that traffic near Road 368 in Sabana Grande is being affected due to a fallen power pole in front of a residence near Hogar Crea. Wind gust around that time ranged around 20 and 22 mph.

The 911 Call Center reported three fallen electrical poles obstructing the roadway at kilometer 4.7 on PR-420 in Barrio Plata, Moca. The incident is preventing residents from exiting the area; however, there are no reports of individuals trapped or injured at this time.

The 911 Call Center reported a fallen tree on PR-901, near Parador Maunacaribe in Barrio Emajagua, Sector Corea in Maunabo. The tree is in contact with electrical cables in the vicinity of a residence; however, there are no reports of individuals trapped or injured at this time.
A 911 caller reported that traffic on Road 774 in Comeri��o is being affected due to a fallen power pole on the main road leading into a residential area.

The 911 Call Center reported a fallen tree in the patio of a residence on PR-173 in Barrio Montellano, near Hacienda Napoles. The tree brought down electrical cables. No individuals are trapped or injured at this time.
A 911 caller reported that traffic on Road 308 after Walgreens and Propper International in Camino los Fas is being affected due to a fallen power pole.
The 911 call center reported that on Road 402 in Anasco, near the municipal garage is being affected due to a fallen power pole.
The 911 Call Center reported a fallen tree obstructing the roadway on PR-2 near Valle de Coloso. There are no individuals trapped, and no electrical wires are present in the area.
A 911 reporter informed that the traffic near road 417 in Aguada is being affected due to power pole that fell in front of a house near Escuela Los Guabanos.
Road PR-3, near radio station Radio Unidad Cristiana 890 AM in Barrio Santiago y Lima, was closed due flooding.

The 911 Call center reported street flooding along Avenida Tito Castro near La Rambla Shopping Center, before Burger King. The flooding affected the roadway, with two vehicles impacted, but no stranded individuals were reported.
The 911 Call Center reported a fallen tree blocking the roadway at km 5.6, PR-368, Bo. La Torre obstructed traffic.

The 911 Call Center reported a fallen utility pole on Cll J7, Ba Playa, near the La Playita sector. The pole was blocking the roadway with power and telephone lines hanging low, though no injuries or property damage were reported.
The 911 Call Center reported a fallen utility pole at Cll 7, Urb. Tintillo Gardens. The pole fell into the yard of a residence near a swimming pool.

Emergency Managers reported a landslide at PR-8827 near De Valencia and Serenata streets (Palacios Reales Urb.) and also near a Retirement Home and Palacios de Versalles Recreational Area. No one was reported as trapped or affected.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS OF SOUTHERN PUERTO RICO OUT 10 NM
events.event_narrative: A member of the public shared a video on social media showing a waterspout observed from the Guanica boardwalk.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS OF NORTHERN PUERTO RICO OUT 10 NM
events.event_narrative: Broadcast media shared on social media photos and videos of a waterspout over the northwestern coastal waters of Puerto Rico, seen from Ramey Base.

The 911 Call Center reported that three males and one female were trapped in the Rio Prieto area. There were no reported injuries; the individuals were stranded due to flooding conditions. All four individuals were rescued safely. A flash flood warning was in effect at the time of the incident, with an estimated 2 to 3 inches of rainfall in the area.
OMME Naguabo reported an overflowing creek affecting a portion of PR-974, near its  intersection with PR-973 and PR-9973. The road was left impassable.
Road PR-4486 is impassable due to flooding from an overflowing small creek, a tributary of the Ri��o Camuy (River), near km 10.7 in Barrio Cibao, Camuy.
A flooded Port St and Mt Welcome Rd in the Gallows Bay area were reported by emergency managers and the media. One trapped vehicle at the intersection near Anally Insurance was observed on video.

Debris flow due to heavy rains was reported at the Aloy Wenty Nielsen Bypass (VI-66). This debris flow occured between the Bypass Overlook and the Intersection with Hospital St and East End Rd. The debris was reported to have been removed around 10 AM.
Emergency managers reported flooding affecting the Ruby M. Ross Housing Complex between the Vester Gade and Valmy Thomas Lane.
Emergency managers reported flooding affecting Downtown Christiansted between King Cross St and Kongens Gade, just in front of Metro Food and the Alexander Hamilton Plaque.
A road was closed due to a landslide in PR-140 km 39.1. The falling rocks made the road impassable.

A 24-year-old male was swept away from the waterfall pool known as Infinity Pool in El  Yunque by a surge of water, fell from a height of 80 feet and died. He was with three other people who are safe.

A member of the public reported on social media that excessive runoff from ongoing rainfall and a nearby river has affected the neighborhood road in Sector La Charca, Barrio Saltos, Orocovis. The road was impassable.

Emergency managers reported two landscape workers swept away by the current in PR-2 (Jose Joaquin Yiye Avila St.), right in front of Las Cascadas Waterpark near Villa Alegria Urbanization. One of the workers had to be transported to a hospital. Their two tractors were also swept away. Flooding was also reported by the media and a NWS Employe along PR-2 (Jose Joaquin Yiye Avila St.) toward GT Tune & Lube.
Emergency Management Director reported that  PR-31, from sector La Pitina to exit 22 of  Expressway PR-53, was impassable and closed  due to flooding from heavy rain and from  nearby Rio Blanco.

Heavy rainfall caused Quebrada Los Muertos to overflow its banks, leading to flooding across PR-444 in Bo. Cuchillas. Video evidence shows water flowing over the roadway while at least one vehicle was observed crossing through the floodwaters.
A report from 911 indicated that Road 177 in Cupey, near the Universidad Interamericana Recinto Metro, is affected by ponding of water on the roadway.

Strong winds associated with a thunderstorm caused multiple trees to fall in the Sector El Tanque, Barrio Arenales Altos. At least one vehicle was damaged by a large tree, and several roads were blocked by debris. No injuries were reported.

A School Bus drove into a flooded Avenida Las Palmas (Avenue) between sectors Amelia and Vietnam in northern Guaynabo. The school bus broke down and remained stranded with the driver and more than 10 children inside. Police officers rescued the passengers; no one was injured.
Flooding was reported at the intersection between Avenida Tte. Cesar Luis Gonzalez (Avenue) and Calle Soldado Hector Salaman (Street). No stranded people or vehicles were reported.
Public sent a picture of a thin Funnel Cloud, observed from the Interamerican University in Aguadilla, that lasted up to 2 minutes.
A member of the public reported on social media that runoff and ponding of water in the urban area of Jayuya near Breban Beauty Supply. The road has flooding but is not impassable.
A 911 reporter informed us that there was some flooding in Barrio Helechal in road PR-162 near El Deportivo Bar. The road was not impassable.
A member of the public shared a video on social media showing a funnel cloud in Barrio Unibon, Parcelas Ramon Pabon.
Impassable road due to flooding at PR-2 between km 52.0 and 52.4 from Manati to Barceloneta. Two lanes were closed.
Fallen Trees and downed electric cables were reported at PR-149 near Jaguas Bakery and  The Burger Hot Spot.

A large tree fell blocking portions of PR-149 at Barrio Jagas in Ciales. The downed tree obstructed traffic but no injuries were reported. Event associated with a strong thunderstorm producing gusty winds and lightning.
A 911 reporter informed us that a tree fell onto the power lines in Bo. Pozas along Road 615 in Ciales. A strong thunderstorm affecting the area produced winds estimated at 20 to 25 mph.
A fallen tree was reported over power lines on Bo. Real Anon, Road 511. The incident occurred while a thunderstorm was moving through the area.
Emergency Managers reported a fallen tree on Avenida Mu��oz Rivera, near the Tribunal de Primera Instancia in San Juan. At the time of the incident, a strong thunderstorm was moving across the area.

Following heavy rains earlier in the afternoon, a landslide occurred along PR-4444 at km 1.0 in Barrio Cuchillas, Sector Loperena. Local authorities reported debris covering the roadway, prompting a temporary closure. Barricades and caution tape were placed to restrict traffic.

A landslide was reported at PR-623 near the bridge over Rio Tanama (River). Emergency managers reported that seven homes were cut off, as this was their only exit. Excavators were brought in to remove the debris before 8:30 p.m.

Emergency managers reported flooding affecting the exit from Expreso Rafael Martinez Nadal toward Avenida Gonzalez Giusti/San Patricio Village, in front of the Dennis Restaurant near Plaza San Patricio in Guaynabo. The roadway has been closed and is currently impassable for all traffic.
Social media posts reported flooding along Avenida 65 de Infanteria in front of Concordia Shopping Center.
Emergency managers reported a small landslide at PR-833 near Urb. La Lomita in Sector Los Filtros in Barrio Frailes.

Emergency managers report runoff and flooding on Road 111, in front of LarCoop near Residencial Jardines de Utuado and the Emergency Management office. Roads remain  passable, with about 3 inches of rainfall were recorded at the time of the report.
A member of the public posted an image on social media of a fallen power pole struck by  lightning during thunderstorm activity in Bo. Saltos, Sector La Charca in Orocovis.
Emergency managers report a landslide affecting both lanes of Road 111 at km 55.2, near Papin Grocery Store and Bar in Utuado.

A social media post showed a landslide along PR-123 at km 28.5 in Adjuntas that sent rocks and debris onto the road, causing a partial closure. The event was attributed to heavy showers in recent days in the mountainous region.
Emergency managers reported through social media a landslide on PR-106, km 8.8 in Mayaguez, route to Las Marias and Maricao. Road closed while DTOP technical team evaluated the situation.
Flooding was reported in the intersection of Moscu St. and Barcelona St. in Olympic Ville Par Pools. A person was stranded in the flooding.
Road PR-937 at km 0.6 in Las Piedras was partially closed due landslide.
Flooding was reported along a marginal street near PR-2, in front of a lumberyard store.
Social media reported flooding and impassable roads at Avenida Luis Vigoreaux and Calle Sirio as Quebrada Margarita reached minor flood stage.
Broadcast media reported impassable roads at San Alfonso Avenue, near Wendys, Reyes Pharmacy #3.
Flooding was reported at PR-175, around km 10.5, between Rio Grande de Loiza (river) and Urb. El Conquistador. Part of the road was still passable, according to video footage.

A police officer was struck by lightning at the Policia de Puerto Rico: Comandancia Regional de Utuado. The officer was standing outside the building, sheltering under an umbrella, when he was struck by lightning.

Flooding was reported over a poorly drained area of Calle E near Quebrada Negrito (creek), Sector Las Pozas Kennedy Hills, Barrio Quebrada Negrito, Trujillo Alto. A vehicle attempted to cross the flooded area and became stranded.
Social media post reported strong winds at Ferreteria Los Nietos y Gelson Window Tint in Sector Ojo de Agua, Barrio Algarrobo.
A landslide and vegetation material slide was blocking traffic on PR-119 (Las Marias St. - San German), Km 70.7.
A landslide was reported at PR-613, km 6.2, in Barrio Tetuan, eastern Utuado. The road was impassable; law enforcement and emergency managers urged citizens to take alternate routes.
A social media publication showed a small tree knocked down at PR-105 km 8. Estimated  wind gusts were around 20-25 mph.
A large tree was uprooted and fell, impacting electrical lines. This caused a power outage in a residential area near Centro Medico.
A large tree fell across PR-361 obstructing traffic and a nearby residence.
A utility pole fell at the entrance of a residence in PR-140 km 20 in Bo Las Palmas.  Blocking the roadway and leaving power lines  hanging across the pavement.
A utility pole was reported down in the middle of the roadway along PR-713, Simarrona, near Rancho Guayama. Electrical cables were hanging across the pavement,  initially obstructing traffic.
Rio Cotui went out of its banks, flooding portions of PR-372 in Yauco. A car was washed out with a male inside, the male was later found dead.

Flooding was reported on Highway PR-100, from the traffic light at the Cabo Rojo COOP to the intersection with the Santa Ana funeral home. PR-100 in the Mayag��ez to Cabo Rojo direction and the secondary road are completely impassable.

A broadcast media outlet reported via social media flooding caused by poor drainage and  clogged sewers on PR-308 in Barrio Miradero, Sector Puerto Real, in front of the Puerto  Rico Police Departments Cabo Rojo District  station.  At that time, radar estimates indicated that 2.0 to 2.2 inches of rain had fallen.

Emergency managers confirmed flooding along PR-31 and PR-53 at exit 22 in Barrio Rio  Blanco in Naguabo due to Rio Blanco (river) overflowing its banks. They proceeded to  close the roads as they were impassable.
Social media post reported Rio Viejo out of its banks in the intersection of PR-103 and  PR-3311. Road was impassable.

A report was received via social media indicating that PR-301, at the intersection with Camino Las Guanbanas, was completely flooded with standing water due to heavy rains. No stranded vehicles were reported.
Social media posts reported flooding along Avenida 65 de Infanteria in front of Concordia Shopping Center.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS OF NORTHERN PUERTO RICO OUT 10 NM
events.event_narrative: A waterspout was reported over Lago Guajataca in Quebradillas. No impacts or damage were reported.

At approximately 12:05 PM AST, a lightning strike occurred at Condominio San Cipriani in Carolina. A 53-year-old male was exiting his vehicle while holding an umbrella when lightning struck his left arm. The individual sustained injuries and was transported to a regional hospital, where he was reported to be in stable condition. No additional injuries or property damage were reported.

The 911 Call Center reported that a tree struck by lightning fell along Avenida Baldorioty in Carolina, just past Plaza Carolina. The fallen tree landed on a vehicle, causing a roadway obstruction. No injuries were reported.

Emergency management officials reported that thunderstorm winds downed a tree near kilometer 4.3 on Road 342 in the Soledad sector of Mayag��ez. The fallen tree partially blocked the roadway. No injuries or additional damage were reported.
Broadcast media shared user-submitted photos and videos showing a funnel cloud observed between the municipalities of Gu��nica and Sabana Grande. No touchdowns or associated damage were reported.
Strong thunderstorm winds caused a large tree to fall, blocking vehicular traffic along Camino La Cueva in Sector Vega Alegre, Bo Monte Grande.

Flooding was reported at the intersection of Camino Vecinal and PR-156 near the Plaza San Crist��bal Shopping Center and Licenciado Bar in Barranquitas. The intersection was impassable due to high water. No structural damage or injuries were reported.
Emergency management reported that a lightning strike impacted a power pole and associated electrical lines along Calle 59 in the Rexville area of Bayam��n. No injuries were reported.
A trained weather spotter reported a lightning strike on a pine tree in Vega Baja. No injuries or additional damage were reported.
State officials reported flooding along PR-2 near Hospital Wilma N. V��zquez in Vega Baja. Water covered portions of the roadway, impacting traffic.

Flooding was reported along sections of PR-887 in Carolina, including areas near Rooms To Go, Freshmart, and a municipal office. Water covered portions of the roadway, affecting traffic flow near the Texaco gas station intersection.

Members of the public reported that a pine tree was struck by lightning along PR-878 near Beltran Auto Parts in Naranjito. The lightning strike damaged the tree, breaking several branches and affecting the trunk.

Broadcast media shared a video from the public showing standing floodwaters along Calle San Antonio in the Floral Park neighborhood of San Juan. Portions of the roadway were covered by water, impacting traffic.

Broadcast media shared a video from the public showing water ponding in poor drainage areas along Calle Dr. Jos�� E. Arrar��s in the Mayag��ez Terrace area of Mayag��ez. Water covered portions of the roadway, affecting traffic.

Broadcast media shared a video from the public showing pea-sized hail in the Santa Rosa I area of Guaynabo. The hail occurred during a strong thunderstorm. No injuries or damage to structures, vehicles, or vegetation were reported.

Emergency management officials reported coastal flooding along PR-187 in the Pi��ones area of Lo��za. Seawater and sand were pushed onto the roadway near Vac��a Talega and the Restauradores Bridge, impacting traffic.

A 72-year-old male surfer was found unresponsive in the water near Playa Tres Palmas in Rinc��n. The individual was struck by his surfboard, lost consciousness, and subsequently drowned in the presence of high surf and strong currents. Bystanders and authorities recovered the victim, who was later pronounced deceased.
Emergency management officials reported flash flooding along Calle San Thomas in Ponce. Heavy rainfall caused the roadway to flood, rendering it impassable.

Emergency management officials reported flooding in the Mar��a Antonia area of Gu��nica. Heavy rainfall caused floodwaters to cover multiple roadways, including Calle Jos�� Nasario and Sim��n Mej��as, rendering them impassable. No injuries or structural damage were reported.

State officials reported that thunderstorm winds caused electrical lines to fall onto the roadway along PR-368 near kilometer 8.5 in the Sus��a Alta area of Yauco. The downed lines obstructed traffic and were in close proximity to nearby residences.

The 911 Call Center reported that a tree fell onto a residence in the Santo Domingo area of Pe��uelas. The fallen tree brought down power lines, resulting in a power outage affecting the surrounding area.

State officials reported that thunderstorm winds caused a large tree branch to fall onto Road 308 near the Playita Ostiones access in Cabo Rojo. The fallen debris blocked the roadway and disrupted traffic.
The 911 Call Center reported that thunderstorm winds caused a tree to fall onto the roadway in Bayam��n, blocking traffic near the Amigo supermarket. The obstruction disrupted traffic flow.
A tree fell and obstructed the roadway along km 8.7 of road 112 towards Moca and the area after Junker P��rez. The incident caused partial blockage of the roadway.
A utility pole fell onto the roadway along Carr. 311 in the Bo. Plan Bonito sector near the area after the basketball court. Power lines were reported hanging over the pavement.
A vehicle became stranded with one person inside due to flooding on PR-100 in front of Baskin Robbins.

A video in social media shows urban street flooding in Ave Luis Munoz Rivera with |several inches of standing water covering multiple travel lanes. Vehicles were observed |continuing to pass through the flooded roadway, indicating the road was not impassable, though traffic was impacted.
Broadcast meteorologist shared on social media a photo of flooding along PR-1, by the port in Old San Juan. The roads were still passable.
Flooding was reported along Avenida Simon Madera near Mall of San Juan. Floodwaters impacted at least one vehicle, with reports of occupants stranded inside.
Residential flooding was reported in Calle B, Estancias Campo Llano in San Juan. Floodwaters impacted one residence.

Flooding was affecting a large parking lot adjacent to the San Juan Weather Forecast Office. Despite ponding, the area remained passable. Radar estimated rainfall totals were approximately 1 to 2 inches.
Flooding was reported along the roadway Calle San Lino at the end of Urb. Sagrado Corazon in Cupey. Floodwaters impacted the roadway, but no vehicles or people were stranded.

The police marine unit and emergency managers reported that a 39-year-old man drowned after being caught in a rip current behind Mar-Bella Restaurant in Loiza. A woman was also swept by the rip current at the same location but was successfully rescued by the first responders.
A tree fell onto power lines on road 162 in the Cuyon sector.
A tree fell and blocked road 7707 behind the correctional facility.
Flooding was reported along Seul street in Las Piedras. A residence was affected by flood waters, with four people trapped inside. No injuries were reported.
The public reported through images and video flooding along roads 114 and 103 in Cabo Rojo, near Hormigueros in sector la Bajura.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS EAST OF PUERTO RICO, AROUND VIEQUES, AND AROUND AND JUST NORTH OF CULEBRA AND SAINT JOHN
events.event_narrative: OMME director from Fajardo reported a waterspout sighted from PR-53. The waterspout was located just offshore of Ceiba, just east Roosevelt Roads.

A report of brief, strong winds not associated with a thunderstorm was received. |Residential solar panels sustained damage, and several trash cans were displaced in the Santa Elena neighborhood in Guayanilla. A resident reported loud wind noise at the time of the event.

Coastal flooding occurred in Aguadilla during the early afternoon of February 2, 2026. An emergency manager reported flooding along Paseo Real Marina and Paseo Col��n, where seawater inundated low-lying coastal areas. Parque Col��n was closed due to the flooding. The event was caused by large breaking waves associated with a long-period northerly swell.

Coastal flooding occurred along PR-102 (Guanajibo Boulevard) near the mouth of the Guanajibo River in Mayag��ez during the morning of February 3, 2026. High surf caused waves to break over the shoreline and inundate the roadway, leaving debris, including small to large tree branches, across the street. Emergency managers responded to the scene and conducted debris removal operations. The flooding was associated with large breaking waves generated by a long-period northerly swell.

Coastal flooding occurred near La Palmita Beach in Barceloneta during the afternoon of February 9, 2026. Emergency managers reported that water and debris covered portions of Road 681 due to wave run-up from large swells. The flooding impacted the roadway and required cleanup operations. The event was caused by large breaking waves associated with a long-period northerly swell.

Emergency managers reported a large fallen tree onto a house in San Isidro, Canovanas. No significant structural damage to the house was reported at the time of the incident. The incident was due to strong winds. Surface observations near the area showed wind gusts between 20 and 28 mph.

High surf impacted the Cueva del Indio area in Arecibo during the afternoon of February 9, 2026. Three individuals were on coastal rocks when a large breaking wave swept them into the ocean. One person returned safely to shore, while the other two were carried offshore. After several days of search operations, the bodies of the two individuals were recovered. The incident was caused by dangerous wave action associated with a long-period northerly swell.

Coastal flooding and erosion occurred in Parcelas Su��rez in R��o Grande during the morning of February 10, 2026. Swell-driven wave action caused significant erosion, leading to the collapse of the intersection at Calle 3 and Calle 10 in Lo��za. The damage impacted roadway infrastructure and surrounding areas. The event was caused by large breaking waves associated with a long-period northerly swell.

Emergency Managers reported a fallen tree at PR-414 at Bo. Guayabo close to the sixth house near the entrance of Bo. Cruces. Emergency managers reported that the roadway was not obstructed but that people were trapped and a person was injured. The nearest official station reported a gust of 25 mph at the time.

At approximately 5:45 PM AST, a well-defined funnel cloud was observed and captured on video by the public in Barrio Piletas, Lares. Video confirmed clear rotation; however, the circulation remained aloft and did not make contact with the surface. No damage or injuries were associated with this convective feature.

A rip current incident occurred at Puerto Nuevo Beach in Vega Baja during the morning of February 19, 2026. Four individuals entered the water and were swept toward deeper waters by a strong rip current. Three individuals returned safely to shore, while one was carried offshore. Search efforts continued for more than a week; however, the individual was not recovered and was classified as missing and presumed dead. This fatality was attributed to hazardous marine conditions associated with a long-period northerly swell.

A landslide occurred along PR-123 in the Saltillo neighborhood of Adjuntas during the morning of February 2, 2026. Emergency managers reported that rainfall between 1 and 3 inches triggered slope failure, resulting in debris covering the roadway and downed trees in the area. The landslide disrupted traffic on the roadway and required clearing operations.

Non-thunderstorm winds caused minor damage in San Sebasti��n during the late morning of February 2, 2026. A fallen tree partially obstructed PR-119 near kilometer 30 in Barrio Hoya Mala, in the vicinity of a gas station. The incident impacted roadway access and required removal operations.

A portion of Santiago Palmer Sur Street in Guayama was closed after heavy rainfall caused the collapse of a brick wall in the area. Based on radar estimates, between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in the area during the day. For safety reasons, the damaged structure was removed, and work was carried out in the zone. Authorities urged the public to avoid the area.
Emergency managers reported that Flooding was occurring in Sector Galateo due to Rio Grande near El Verde being out of its banks impacting PR-956, near km 0.5. The road was impassable.
People were trapped in their vehicle due to flash flooding in road R887 KM 2.2 San Anton.

The 911 call center reported that emergency managers responded to flooding at the intersection of PR-317 and PR-114 in San German. Floodwaters inundated the roadway, resulting in persons stranded in at least one vehicle.
Flood waters affected Calle San Lino, near the baseball park in Urb Sagrado Corazones.
Road PR-119 intersection with PR-453 at sector Las Palmas, Barrio Guajataca, was flooded and impassable due to Quebrada La Margarita out of its banks. The road was closed by the local authorities.
Flood waters were entering a residence at road PR-834, km 0.7, in Sector Estrella in Barrio Guaraguao.
Road PR-798 in Sector Salchichon in Barrio Rio Canas was completely flooded and impassable due to Rio Canas out of its banks.
Rio Blanco went out of its banks, flooding portions of PR-31, Km 8.0, exit 22 in Naguabo. Road was impassable and closed by authorities.

Flooding was reported at Ramiro Rivera Bridge in Barrio Bauta Abajo, Sector La Francia, Orocovis due to a Rio Matrullas tributary out of its banks. The bridge was impassable. Broadcast Media and Emergency Managers confirmed that the bridge was once again passable by around 7 PM.

Flooding over a low-level bridge along PR-372 near the conjunction of Rio Yauco and Rio Duey in Barrio Diego Hernandez Sector Cotui, due to river rise. USGS sensor at Rio Yauco reported action stage level (up to 7.14 feet).

Flooding was reported at PR-101 between the municipal border of San German and Lajas and the intersection of PR-318. Video footage showed the flooded roadway with several vehicles crossing with difficulty while avoiding deeper floodwaters.
OMME director reported flooding on Pacifico Street ext. Punto Oro near a Walmart Supercenter.
An official municipal account posted photos of a flooded Rafael D. Milan Padro stadium, including the baseball park, dugout and the racetrack. The stadium was closed.

Broadcast media through social media reported that heavy rainfall resulted in water flowing over the roadway at the entrance to PR-328 toward Rayo Guaras in Sabana Grande. The flooding created hazardous driving conditions.

Flooding was reported in the Las Guaras sector of Sabana Grande near the municipal boundary with Lajas. Heavy runoff caused muddy water to flow rapidly over roadways, creating hazardous driving conditions.

A fallen tree was reported as obstructing PR-605 near kilometer marker 3.3 in Barrio Vivi Arriba near a local school. This fallen tree also affected nearby power lines. Due to the obstructed roadway and power line damage, the section of PR-605 will remain closed until repairs can be completed and the tree is removed.
Emergency management officials reported a fatality associated with rip currents in Punta Arenas Beach, Vieques.
Two persons were swept away by rip currents at Poza de las Mujeres Beach along road PR-6684.
A man drowned after being swept away by rip currents at Condado Beach in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The man lost his life when he entered the water to rescue two of his friends.

Three people were swept away by rip currents along the coast of Luquillo, just behind the La Parrilla establishment. All three individuals were rescued from the water. Two survived the incident, while one person was transported to a hospital in Fajardo, where the individual was later pronounced dead due to drowning.

Rain bands moving across central Puerto Rico produced gusty winds that downed a tree and a utility pole onto PR-156 near Bayamoncito. The fallen debris blocked the roadway near kilometer 41.1, resulting in a temporary road closure. Law enforcement managed the incident, and the roadway was later reopened. Nearby observations indicated winds between 15 and 22 mph, with locally stronger gusts within the rain activity estimated near 40 mph.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS OF SOUTHERN PUERTO RICO OUT 10 NM
events.event_narrative: Strong winds and rough seas caused a small recreational vessel carrying four occupants to capsize near Caja de Muerto, south of Ponce. One person drowned while three others were rescued and survived the incident. Hazardous marine conditions were present across the local waters due to enhanced easterly winds associated with a strong Atlantic high-pressure system.

A pilot submitted an urgent PIREP while flying at approximately 3,500 feet and reported a funnel cloud over the Atlantic waters north of Puerto Rico. The funnel cloud was observed approximately 12 nautical miles northwest of the aircraft's position, near 5 miles north of Dorado. No surface impacts, damage, injuries, or fatalities were reported.

Heavy rainfall produced a rapid rise in water levels at the Puente El Coqu�� low-water crossing along a tributary of the Guayan��s River. Floodwaters overtopped the crossing, creating hazardous travel conditions. No injuries, fatalities, or property damage were reported.

Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding at Ernesto Ramos Antonini School in Yauco. Floodwaters accumulated rapidly on the school grounds, causing flooding in the affected area. No injuries, fatalities, or evacuations were reported. The flooding was associated with intense rainfall that affected portions of southwestern Puerto Rico.

Heavy rainfall triggered flash flooding in southern Yauco, inundating portions of Roads 127 and 128. The roads became impassable, resulting in hazardous travel conditions and temporary transportation disruptions. No injuries, fatalities, or structural damage were reported.

Heavy rainfall caused rapid rises along a tributary crossing PR-5516 in Adjuntas. Floodwaters overtopped a bridge located between Selecto Supermarket and the Sweet and Frozen business, making the roadway impassable and disrupting local travel. No injuries or fatalities were reported.

Heavy rainfall caused R��o Loco to rise rapidly, flooding portions of Road 335 in Barrio Barina. The roadway became impassable and was temporarily closed to traffic, causing transportation disruptions in the area. No injuries, fatalities, or structural damage were reported.

Heavy rainfall caused a river to overflow onto PR-891 near kilometer 13.9 by the Volleyball Monument in Corozal. Floodwaters covered the roadway, forcing the closure of the road in both directions after it became impassable. The flooding resulted in temporary transportation disruptions, but no injuries, fatalities, or structural damage were reported.

Heavy rainfall caused a river to overflow onto PR-818 in Barrio Cibuco near the sewage treatment facilities in Corozal. Floodwaters covered the roadway, forcing its closure in both directions after it became impassable. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
Heavy rainfall caused a river to overflow at Puente Bull in Naranjito. Floodwaters overtopped the roadway, forcing its closure in both directions after it became impassable.

Heavy rainfall caused a creek to overflow in Sector Paracaochero near Camino Los Cruces in San Juan. Flash floodwaters inundated two residential units near Aceros de Am��rica, resulting in flood damage to the affected properties. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
Heavy rainfall caused the R��o Cibuco to overflow and inundate portions of PR-675 in Vega Alta. Floodwaters covered the roadway, making it impassable and disrupting travel through the area.

Heavy rainfall caused the R��o Cibuco to overflow, resulting in flash flooding across multiple roadways in Vega Alta. Floodwaters inundated portions of PR-620, PR-647, PR-675, PR-690, and PR-676, creating hazardous travel conditions and temporary transportation disruptions. Debris and sediment deposited by the floodwaters required cleanup operations before affected roadways could safely reopen.

Persistent heavy rainfall caused the R��o Cibuco to overflow its banks near the PR-2 interchange at Exit 22 in Vega Alta. Floodwaters inundated the highway, rendering portions of the roadway impassable and disrupting transportation along a major traffic corridor.

Persistent heavy rainfall caused the R��o Cibuco to overflow its banks near PR-160 approaching PR-2 in Vega Baja. Floodwaters inundated the roadway, rendering it impassable and stranding several motorists. Emergency response actions were required to address the hazardous conditions and assist affected travelers. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
Flood waters were affecting a parking lot of a building near a dairy corporation. Several cars were parked over the parking area.
A car was stranded with a person inside due to flooding waters at exit to pr-22 toward avenue Jose de Diego.
Flood waters affected a house in 124 Ponce de Leon and nearby areas. Standing water was observed inside the first floor of the house.
Gusty winds from a thunderstorm resulted in downed trees that brought down electrical lines onto the roadway obstructing traffic near PR-455 KM 12.
Floodwaters from Rio Culebrinas impacted PR-110 KM 9.9 near Valle Encantado in sector Los Cocos. At the time, the USGS river sensor measured 22.4 ft.
Emergency managers reported flooding along PR-676 KM 1.6, near Mariposario Bosque la Vega in Vega Alta.
Emergency managers reported flooding along PR-2 near Ileana de Gracia high school.

Emergency managers reported floodwaters along PR-2 near Mayaguez Mall. Flooding was observed in both directions, from Mayag��ez to Hormigueros and vice versa. Vehicles were still moving, but there was water accumulating on the roadway. Based on radar estimates, around 2 inches of rain fell.

Water from a small creek was overflowing into a rural road in sector Rabo del Buey, near road PR-165 and before Camino Kilometro 9.8.

Broadcast media reported on social media that Higuera creek between Barrio Palomas and Barrio Dona Elena is out of its banks. Based on radar estimates between 3 to 4.5 inches of rain had fallen at the time of the report.
Emergency managers reported flooding impacting a house. It is uncommunicated due to a nearby landslide in PR-780 km 4.8 in Barrio Dona Elena, Comerio.

County officials posted on social media, and emergency managers then confirmed, two |landslides on PR-7780 between kilometers 3.1 and 3.5 in Barrio Dona Elena, Comeri��o. The road was impassable. Based on radar estimates, between 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain had fallen in that area at the time of the report.

County officials reported on social media a landslide due to recent rainfall in PR-466 in Barrio Bajuras, Isabela. Based on radar estimates, around 2 to almost 4 inches of rain fell in that area at the time of the report.

County officials reported on social media a landslide due to recent rainfall in PR-749 kilometer 2.3 in Barrio Quebrada Grande, Barranquitas. The road was impassable.
A landslide was reported at PR-780 near El Rejon del Gallo, affecting the roadway. The roadway was not reported as impassable.
Flooding was reported at PR-132 km 14.4 near El Resbalon Bar and Restaurant in Bo. Tallaboa Alta.

Emergency managers reported flooding along a poorly drained area of PR-132 in Barrio Canas, Ponce. The road was still passable. Radar estimates indicate that approximately 1 to 2 inches of rainfall occurred in the area at the time of the report.

Street flooding reported on Calle A in Barrio Palomas near a local church at the intersection with Callejon Viqueira. Water is observed covering the roadway and reaching the chassis level of parked vehicles.
A social media post showed what appears to be a small creek overflowing and impacting the entrance and exit of Playa Buye, preventing people from leaving the area.

PR-31 near PR-53 exit 22 impassable due to Rio Blanco out of its banks. The USGS sensor reported 7.91 feet at 7:30 AM AST.

Emergency managers reported that a landslide occurred along PR-348 km 14.6. The roadway was partially obstructed.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS OF SOUTHERN PUERTO RICO OUT 10 NM
events.event_narrative: A video shared on social media showed a waterspout just offshore of Maunabo.

High surf conditions led to an incident today in which two people were walking over a rock formation near the natural pools at Poza Las Mujeres Beach. A wave swept one person into the water. Emergency Management personnel successfully rescued the other individual, while the search for the missing person continued for two days until the body was recovered.

The municipal police, maritime unit, of San Juan rescued a 34-year-old female tourist from Maryland after she was dragged out to  the sea by a rip current at Condado Beach. The incident occurred during high season surveillance. The victim was assisted by emergency personnel and reported in stable condition with no injuries.

Two rescue divers were injured at La Poza de las Mujeres after being struck by a large wave, thrown against rocks, and swept away by strong rip currents during a recovery operation. The divers suffered various fractures and trauma. The incident occurred amid adverse marine conditions and strong surf, hampering recovery efforts for a 24-year-old male who was swept away by currents on Thursday. The injured divers were rescued from the water by a police helicopter (FURA) and transported to a medical center in stable condition.

The 911 Call Center reported two females were rescued after being swept by water currents near Carr. 187 behind the Courtyard Marriott in Carolina. Both individuals were safely removed from the water, and medical services were offered on scene.

events.event_narrative: A waterspout was reported between Humacao and Vieques.

Heavy rains that began on Christmas evening persisted through early Christmas Day. Around 250 families were affected by the rains and floods. The worst hit area was the Aibonito town and the San Luis sector. Many homes close to the river and the town were flooded, as well as Barrios La Plata, Pasto, and Cuyon. Flood water levels rose to around 3 feet in some of the properties. USGS river gauge at Rio de la Plata at Proyecto La Plata rose above flood stage to 18.77 feet. Twenty seven persons were rescued from the flash floods.

events.cz_name: COASTAL WATERS OF SOUTHERN PUERTO RICO OUT 10 NM
events.event_narrative: LPRP4 Mesonet station southeast of Ponce near the Caja de Muertos island recorded a wind gust of 40 mph from the east southeast as a squall line moved west northwest.

The Penuelas Guayanilla NOS NWLON weather sensor recorded sustained winds of 41 mph with gusts to 53 mph from the south at 12:17 PM, as a squall line moved west northwest. Sustained winds from 33-38 mph with gusts between 38-47 mph were recorded between 12:27 -13:08 AST from the south and south southeast.

At Wendy���s restaurant, located at Mandela Circle in St. Thomas, the road in front of the restaurant was flooded. Heavy rains during the afternoon closed St. Thomas' Brookman Road, combined with street flooding near Havensight Mall.

Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms inland between the municipalities of Aibonito and Barranquitas caused a rapid water rise along the Coamo River near road 153, two person riding a four track vehicle were overtaken by the surge, but were rescued later.
